title: A regular stalk map gives a smooth neighborhood under local finite presentation
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] which is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $x\in X$. Write $y=f(x)$ and let $f_x^\sharp:\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ be its induced local homomorphism [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. If $f_x^\sharp$ is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], there exists an open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ containing $x$ such that $f|_U:U\to Y$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

source.place: Tag 01V9 (lemma-smooth-at-point), (2) implies (1), combined with Varieties Tags 038U (lemma-geometrically-regular-at-point) and 038X (lemma-geometrically-regular-smooth) in varieties.tex: geometric regularity of the closed fibre local ring implies smoothness of the finite-type fibre at x.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_y$, and $k=\kappa(y)$. The definition in [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], applied to the prime $\mathfrak m$ of the local ring $A$, gives two facts: $A\to B$ is flat, and $C=B\otimes_A k$ is a Noetherian geometrically regular $k$-algebra. These are consequences of the regular-map hypothesis itself; no flatness on a neighbourhood is asserted.

source.place: Tag 07BZ, definition-regular, flatness and the fibre at the maximal ideal

proof.text: Let $F=X_y$ and let $\xi\in F$ be the point over $x$. By [lem-sbc-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient], $\mathcal O_{F,\xi}\cong B/\mathfrak mB$, by the map induced from the fibre projection. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-localization-quotient] to $A\to B$ at $\mathfrak m$. Every element of $A\setminus\mathfrak m$ is already a unit of $A$, hence maps to a unit of $B$, so the localization of $B$ occurring there is $B$ itself. Its displayed formula identifies $C$ with $B/\mathfrak mB$. These are isomorphisms of $k$-algebras: for $a\in A$, both send the class of $a$ in $k=A/\mathfrak m$ to the class of its image in $B$. Thus $\mathcal O_{F,\xi}$ is geometrically regular over $k$: tensor these isomorphisms with each finite purely inseparable extension of $k$ and use the defining regularity of the corresponding tensor of $C$.

The morphism $F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type. Indeed, around each point $x_0\in X$ with $f(x_0)=y$, choose affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $x_0\in W$, $f(W)\subseteq T$, and $R\to S$ finitely presented, as allowed by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The map $\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$ factors through $T$ since its image is $y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the inverse image of $W$ in $F$ is the affine open $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_R k)$, with its $k$-structure given by the second tensor factor. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition], this is a finitely presented $k$-algebra (interchange tensor factors); in particular its finite list of polynomial generators generates it as a $k$-algebra. These opens cover $F$, proving the assertion by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tags 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product) and 01I4/01JQ (affine fibre products); algebra.tex Tag 05G5 (lemma-base-change-finiteness), (4)

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-geometrically-regular-stalk-smooth-over-field] to $F$ over $k$ at $\xi$. Step 3 verifies local finite type and step 2 verifies geometric regularity of its stalk with the correct $k$-algebra structure. It gives an open neighbourhood of $\xi$ in $F$ smooth over $k$.

Apply [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion] to $f$ at $x$. Local finite presentation is a hypothesis of the item, flatness of the stalk map is step 1, and smoothness of the fibre at the point over $x$ is step 4. Its reverse implication gives an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ on which $f$ is smooth, exactly the conclusion.
